 We’re looking for a Product Design Manager with that combination of creative leadership and personal craft. Someone with strong design judgement, deep visual craft, and the ambition to change what businesses expect from financial software.
 You’ll lead design for Mercury’s Business Banking* and Investments teams, spanning payments, accounts, and treasury. These teams help businesses move money, organize their accounts, and put idle cash to work. As the team grows, you’ll be accountable for the quality of its work, the development of its designers, and the impact of the experiences it ships.
 Our ambition goes beyond making familiar banking workflows look better. We want to question how they work, identify what customers should no longer have to think about, and create something meaningfully better. That takes a leader who can recognize a promising idea, push it further, and bring a team together to make it real.
 Visual design matters deeply in this role. So do interaction design, simplicity, and the judgment to make them work together. You should have a clear point of view about what excellent looks like and the hands-on ability to demonstrate it. You’ll hold a high standard through specific feedback, compelling direction, and a willingness to work alongside the team. People should feel inspired to do the best work of their careers, and supported in getting there.
 In this role, you’ll: 
 Raise the quality bar of the team's work. Own the visual and interaction quality of the experiences your team ships, from the structure of a complex workflow to typography, composition, spacing, and motion. Make the standard concrete through thoughtful critique and clear direction. Review the implemented experience, not just the design file.
 Challenge the status quo. Partner with Product and Engineering to shape an ambitious direction for payments, accounts, and treasury. Question inherited assumptions, including our own. Help the team distinguish genuine constraints from familiar habits, explore alternatives, and turn the strongest ideas into simpler, more useful products.
 Take ownership from problem to outcome. Identify opportunities without waiting for a brief. Create clarity when the path is ambiguous, bring the right people together, make decisions, and work through obstacles. Your responsibility continues after handoff and launch: understand what changed for customers and the business, and act when the results fall short.
 Get hands-on where your craft makes a difference. Sketch a stronger direction, prototype an interaction, or work through a difficult flow with a designer. Be able to show what better looks like, not only describe it. Use your skills selectively to advance the work and develop the designer’s judgment without taking over their ownership.
 Turn ambition into excellent work that ships on time. Make deliberate decisions about scope, sequencing, and where to spend the team’s attention. Surface tradeoffs early and resolve them with your partners. Know which details are essential to the experience and where a simpler approach will help the team move faster without compromising what matters.
 Build a healthy team with high expectations. Develop designers’ taste, confidence, and ability to deliver. Give direct, useful feedback, set clear performance expectations, and address gaps with care and conviction. Explain why the work matters and bring people together around a shared vision. Celebrate the designers behind the work and make their contributions visible across Mercury Design.
 You should: 
 Have strong visual and interaction design craft. Your portfolio demonstrates thoughtful typography, composition, hierarchy, and interaction design in shipped products.
 Know how to simplify complex product experiences. You can work through complicated workflows, information architecture, and product constraints to make experiences clear and intuitive.
 Have managed designers and raised the quality of their work . You can show how your coaching, feedback, and clear expectations helped designers grow and improved what reached customers. You know how to inspire ambition while holding people accountable.
 Have set a product vision and helped a team deliver it. You can connect an ambitious direction to practical decisions about scope and sequencing, with shipped work and clear customer or business impact.
 Stay close to the design work. You’re comfortable sketching, prototyping, and working through detailed design problems alongside designers, with the judgment to know when your direct contribution will help.
 Build strong partnerships with Product and Engineering. You’ve shaped priorities together, worked through competing constraints, and used clear storytelling to build alignment around design decisions.
 Think and work like an owner. You act on what’s best for customers and the business, not just what’s in the brief. You spot problems and opportunities before they’re assigned, make decisions with incomplete information, and adapt without drama when priorities shift. You stay close to implementation and outcomes, and you care more about making Mercury better than about whose idea it was.
 Build conviction without relying on authority. You can tell a clear story about where the product should go and why. You start disagreements with curiosity, make your reasoning specific, and change your mind when a better idea emerges. You help people pursue a demanding standard because they understand and believe in it.
 What success looks like 
 A year from now, the team’s shipped work demonstrates a visibly higher standard of visual craft, interaction quality, and simplicity. It has moved beyond incremental improvements to deliver new approaches with clear customer and business impact. Designers are ambitious, motivated, and growing in their judgment. They own their work, deliver reliably, and receive recognition across Mercury Design for what they contribute.
 Please share examples of both your own design craft and work produced under your leadership. We’d like to understand the standards you set, the assumptions you challenged, the decisions you owned, and what ultimately shipped.

ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

Solutions Consultant, Post-Sales at Ramp partner with Account Management to deepen and expand relationships with existing Ramp customers. You'll act as the technical and financial subject matter expert across the customer lifecycle — running product demonstrations to expand customers onto new Ramp products, while bringing the depth needed to resolve complex ERP integrations, configuration challenges, and technical blockers.

 

You'll collaborate closely with Account Managers to assess requirements, design scalable solutions, and ensure fast time-to-value as customers grow with Ramp. You will partner with Post-Sales teams to drive Product, Design and Engineering teams' roadmaps to evolve Ramp to better serve our customers at scale and offer increasingly higher value to the customers. This role requires strong technical skills — comfort with APIs, ERP systems, and integration architecture — paired with the communication ability to translate complexity into clear business value for finance and operations stakeholders.

 

This role is specifically focused on Strategic Enterprise customers, supporting large, complex organizations with multi-entity environments, advanced ERP integrations, and highly customized financial workflows.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Partner with Account Managers to demonstrate new Ramp products and features to existing customers, building the business case for expansion through customized demos and workflow illustrations

 - Evaluate customer requirements for expansion opportunities, assessing fit through use-case analysis, ROI assessments, and technical scoping

 - Design and recommend best-fit Ramp architecture — including when and how to use APIs, ERP integrations, and HRIS connectors — based on each customer's existing systems and workflows

 - Act as a technical advisor to customers and internal teams, guiding integration, configuration, and system design decisions without writing code directly

 - Troubleshoot ERP and integration blockers, and guide customers through complex configuration decisions across NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle Fusion, and others

 - Support Account Managers on technical workstreams, ensuring faster time-to-value during product rollouts and expansions

 - Be a subject matter expert across accounting systems and integration partners; advocate for integration development in line with customer needs alongside Product and Partners

 - Influence Ramp's product roadmap by channeling customer pain points and feedback to Product and Engineering teams

 - Contribute to internal documentation, tooling, and knowledge bases that scale Ramp's ability to support integration use cases across a growing customer base

WHAT YOU NEED

 - 4+ years in Solutions Consulting, Technical Consulting, Implementation, or a similar customer-facing technical role in SaaS or fintech

 - Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, finance, business, or a related field

 - Hands-on familiarity with ERP systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle Fusion) and finance/accounting workflows

 - Comfort with APIs, integration logic, and system architecture — and the ability to explain those concepts clearly to finance and operations stakeholders

 - Experience running product demonstrations and translating complex technical capabilities into clear business value

 - Strong communication skills: able to guide customers toward scalable approaches and diplomatically steer conversations when requests are misaligned with product capabilities or best practices

 - Collaborative mindset; effective working cross-functionally with Account Management, Product, and Engineering

 - Thrives in ambiguity and fast-paced environments; highly organized, ownership-oriented, and resourceful as Ramp scales its upmarket motion

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend

UNITED STATES

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Pet insurance

   
   

CANADA

 - Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

ABOUT FLOAT

 

 

OUR PRODUCT

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.

 

AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

ABOUT THE ROLE

Float’s partnerships channel is one of our newest growth motions, and the one with the most room to run.

Accounting firms, affiliates and technology platforms already use Float as one place to manage their clients’ financial operations while growing their own. The foundation is strong. The playbook is still unwritten.

As Head of Partnerships, you’ll report into our SVP of GTM and own the partnerships channel end to end: how we find and win partners across all three types, how we build a community that makes them want to stay, and how what they tell us shapes the product roadmap. You’ll take partnerships from promising to a meaningful share of Float’s growth.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

WRITE THE PARTNERSHIP PLAYBOOK

 - Build a multi-year partnership strategy with clear milestones tied to revenue and strategic value.

 - Create the processes, playbooks and infrastructure to scale from a handful of partners to dozens.

 - Set the targets and reporting. You define what a great channel looks like, then hit it.

WIN AND GROW PARTNERS

 - Find, win, activate and grow partners across accounting and bookkeeping firms, fractional finance teams and investor networks.

 - Own the full deal cycle, from first conversation to signed partner.

 - Design one-to-many distribution and enablement programs so one partner relationship reaches hundreds of clients.

 - Start with the firms that bring the most reach, then widen from there. Once a partner is live, work with Sales to accelerate revenue through them.

BUILD THE COMMUNITY

 - Run the programs, events and community that make partners better at their jobs and make serving clients easier.

 - Track what each partner type delivers, and double down on what works.

 - Own how Float shows up for partners, in their language, alongside Marketing.

BRING THE OUTSIDE IN

 - Carry market intelligence and partner feedback back into company strategy and roadmap.

 - Work with internal stakeholders to clear whatever slows partners down.

BUILD THE TEAM

 - Grow a small team, shape it around where the channel is today, and decide where you stay hands-on.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 8+ years in partnerships, channel or ecosystem growth in B2B SaaS, fintech or payments, including building a partner program from the early stage

 - Proven ownership of a partner funnel end to end (sourcing, conversion, activation, expansion) and fluency in the numbers behind each stage

 - Comfort being the public face of a program: building community and representing us with external partners

 - A marketer’s instinct for positioning a product for a specific audience, ideally professional-services firms

 - Experience leading a small team

 - Working knowledge of how accounting and bookkeeping firms operate

 - Willingness to travel regularly across Canada for events and partner visits

 - Strong command of AI tools, as both a user and a builder

 - Nice to haves
   
   - A network in Canadian accounting, bookkeeping, VC or PE circles, or a background as an accountant or bookkeeper
   
   - French proficiency (an asset, not a requirement)

 - You need an established playbook and a large team before you can do your best work.

 - You would rather manage a channel from the sidelines than meet partners yourself.

 - You prefer a narrow, single-function remit. This role spans marketing, sales and product.

 - You're not energized by feedback or fast-paced change.

OUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY

WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN

 - Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team

 - Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits

Who we are
 About Stripe
 Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.
 Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.
 About the team
 Our Data Science team partners deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. We're looking for data scientists with a passion for analyzing data, building machine learning and statistical models, and running experiments to drive impact. Our Fraud, Losses, and Financial Crime Data Science team builds the models and data products that protect Stripe and its users from fraud, account takeover, and financial crime. We own the full fraud and loss modeling stack - from account takeover detection and card fraud classification to merchant-level loss estimation, unsupervised anomaly detection, and financial crime risk modeling. We partner with Fraud Engineering, Financial Crimes Engineering, and Risk Operations to bring these systems into production and ensure they have measurable impact on Stripe's financial integrity and user trust.
 What you’ll do
 As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous data analysts and scientists in the industry. You'll partner deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. You'll work closely with partners to extract insights from the rich and complex data at Stripe. You'll build metrics, scalable data pipelines, dashboards, and reports to inform and run the business. You'll deliver actionable business recommendations through analyses and data storytelling.
 Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high.

 Applying probability distributions, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing to quantify uncertainty and evaluate business outcomes
 Using Python or R for data analysis, data processing, visualizations, statistical modeling, machine learning, predictive analytics, automation, and implementing causal inference and experimental analyses

 Modeling temporal dependencies, seasonality, and trend decomposition to generate and evaluate time-series predictions
 Identifying structural patterns, clusters, and outliers in unlabeled data
 Deploying models in production and adjusting model thresholds to improve performance
 Designing, running, and analyzing complex experiments and leveraging causal inference designs
 Using SQL and Spark to create, transform, and analyze large datasets
 Learn quickly by asking great questions, finding how to work with your mentor and teammates effectively, and communicating the status of your work clearly
 Present your work to the Data Science team, partner teams, and fellow interns.

En mettant l'accent sur la fiabilité, la performance et la responsabilité environnementale, Smardt continue de redéfinir les normes du secteur grâce à une ingénierie de pointe et à son engagement en faveur d'un avenir plus durable.
 Résumé du Rôle 
 Le responsable des achats est chargé de diriger et de superviser les activités d'achat et d'approvisionnement de l'organisation afin de garantir l'acquisition de biens et de services dans les délais, à un coût raisonnable et en conformité avec les réglementations.
Ce poste consiste à élaborer et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d'achat qui optimisent les coûts, la qualité et la performance des fournisseurs, tout en soutenant les objectifs opérationnels et la croissance de l'entreprise. Le responsable des achats collabore étroitement avec des équipes interfonctionnelles, notamment celles chargées des opérations, des finances, des stocks, de la chaîne d'approvisionnement et de la logistique, afin de prévoir les besoins d'achat, d'assurer la continuité des stocks et de répondre aux demandes de production et des clients.
Le poste consiste également à superviser les processus d'approvisionnement, à garantir le respect des politiques de l'entreprise et des réglementations applicables, ainsi qu'à tenir à jour des registres d'achat et des rapports précis.
Le titulaire du poste dirigera et développera l'équipe des achats (5 à 6 employés) afin de favoriser l'excellence opérationnelle et l'amélioration continue.
 Principales Responsabilités 
 Stratégie d'approvisionnement et direction des achats 
 Élaborer, mettre en œuvre et exécuter des stratégies d'achat alignées sur les objectifs opérationnels de l'organisation, les exigences de fabrication et les plans de croissance de l'entreprise.
 Définir les priorités d'approvisionnement, les stratégies d'approvisionnement et les pratiques d'achat qui optimisent les coûts, la qualité, la fiabilité des fournisseurs et l'efficacité des achats.
 Diriger l'élaboration et l'amélioration continue des politiques, procédures, processus et contrôles internes en matière d'achats.
 Identifier les opportunités de regroupement des activités d’achat, de tirage parti des volumes d’achat, de standardisation des matériaux et d’amélioration de l’efficacité des achats.
 Définir les objectifs du service, les cibles de performance et les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) afin de mesurer l’efficacité des achats.
 Opérations et exécution des achats 
 Superviser les activités quotidiennes d’achat, notamment les demandes d’achat, les bons de commande, les confirmations des fournisseurs, le suivi des commandes et le suivi des livraisons.
 Veiller à ce que les activités d’achat soient exécutées avec précision, efficacité et conformément aux pouvoirs d’approbation établis et aux procédures d’approvisionnement de l’entreprise.
 Assurer le traitement en temps opportun des bons de commande afin de répondre aux exigences de production et aux besoins opérationnels.
 Surveiller les bons de commande en cours et les engagements des fournisseurs, en traitant les retards, les divergences et les problèmes en suspens avec les fournisseurs.
 Collaboration interfonctionnelle 
 Collaborer étroitement avec les services de production, d’ingénierie, de qualité, des finances, de gestion des stocks et d’autres départements opérationnels afin de comprendre les besoins en matière d’achats et de s’assurer que les activités d’approvisionnement répondent aux besoins de l’entreprise.
 Travailler avec la production et les équipes de planification concernées pour coordonner les priorités d’achat et s’assurer que les matériaux requis sont commandés conformément aux exigences de production établies.
 Collaborer avec l’ingénierie et la qualité pour garantir que les matériaux et composants achetés respectent les spécifications techniques requises, les normes de qualité et les exigences réglementaires applicables.
 Direction et développement de l’équipe 
 Diriger, encadrer et développer une équipe d’environ cinq à six professionnels des achats, en définissant clairement les responsabilités, les attentes en matière de performance et les obligations de rendre compte.
 Organiser et hiérarchiser les charges de travail du service afin de garantir que les activités d’achat soient alignées sur les exigences opérationnelles et les priorités de l’entreprise.
 Définir des objectifs de performance individuels et départementaux, suivre les résultats et assurer un retour d’information continu ainsi qu’une gestion des performances.
 Identifier les opportunités de formation et de développement afin de renforcer les capacités d’approvisionnement, les compétences en négociation, la gestion des fournisseurs et l’efficacité des achats.
 Rapports, conformité et gestion des risques 
 Élaborer et tenir à jour des rapports et des tableaux de bord relatifs aux achats afin de suivre les dépenses d’approvisionnement, les performances des fournisseurs, les économies réalisées, l’activité des bons de commande et les tendances en matière d’achats.
 Veiller à ce que les activités d’achat respectent les politiques de l’entreprise, les pouvoirs d’approbation établis, les obligations contractuelles et les exigences réglementaires applicables.
 Tenir à jour une documentation d’achat précise et complète pour faciliter les contrôles financiers, les examens internes et les exigences d’audit.

 Ce qui rend ce poste unique 
 Salaires compétitifs 
 Prestations (médicales, dentaires) payées à 100 % des le 1iere jour!

 Soins de santé virtuels TELUS avec accès 24h/7j

 La capacité de communiquer en français avec notre équipe au Québec est importante.
 Nous travaillons dans un environnement multiculturel et international, de solides compétences en anglais sont également requises pour interagir avec nos fournisseurs et notre équipe internationale.

 Smardt is looking to hire a Purchasing Manager to be a part of our team in Dorval! 
 About   SMARDT  
 As a global pioneer in oil-free centrifugal chiller technology with an expanding portfolio of thermal management solutions, Smardt is dedicated to delivering high-efficiency and energy-saving systems for industries, real estate developments, health care and educational centers worldwide. We operate manufacturing facilities in the US, Canada, Germany, China, and Australia, with a team of over 900 employees. With a focus on reliability, performance, and environmental stewardship, Smardt continues to redefine industry standards through advanced engineering and a commitment to a more sustainable future.
 What We're Looking For 
 The Purchasing Manager is responsible for leading and overseeing the organization’s purchasing and procurement activities to ensure the timely, cost-effective, and compliant acquisition of goods and services.
 This role develops and implements purchasing strategies that optimize cost, quality, and supplier performance while supporting operational objectives and business growth. The Purchasing Manager collaborates closely with cross-functional teams including operations, finance, inventory, supply chain, and logistics to forecast purchasing requirements, maintain inventory continuity, and support production and customer demands.
 The role is also responsible for overseeing procurement processes, ensuring compliance with company policies and applicable regulations, maintaining accurate purchasing records and reporting.
 The role will be leading and developing the purchasing team (5-6 employees) to drive operational excellence and continuous improvement.
 This role is 100% on site at our office in Dorval. 
 What You'll Do: 
 Procurement Strategy & Purchasing Leadership 
 Develop, implement, and execute purchasing strategies aligned with the organization's operational objectives, manufacturing requirements, and business growth plans. 
 Establish procurement priorities, sourcing strategies, and purchasing practices that optimize cost, quality, supplier reliability, and purchasing efficiency.
 Lead the development and continuous improvement of purchasing policies, procedures, processes, and internal controls.
 Identify opportunities to consolidate purchasing activities, leverage purchasing volumes, standardize materials, and improve procurement efficiencies.
 Establish departmental objectives, performance targets, and key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure purchasing effectiveness.
 Purchasing Operations & Execution 
 Oversee day-to-day purchasing activities, including purchase requisitions, purchase orders, supplier confirmations, order tracking, and delivery follow-ups.
 Ensure purchasing activities are executed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with established approval authorities and company procurement procedures.
 Ensure timely processing of purchase orders to support production requirements and operational needs.
 Monitor open purchase orders and supplier commitments, addressing delays, discrepancies, and outstanding issues with suppliers.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration 
 Collaborate closely with Production, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Inventory Management, and other operational departments to understand purchasing requirements and ensure procurement activities support business needs.
 Work with Production and relevant planning teams to coordinate purchasing priorities and ensure required materials are ordered in accordance with established production requirements.
 Partner with Engineering and Quality to ensure purchased materials and components meet required technical specifications, quality standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.
 Team Leadership & Development 
 Lead, coach, and develop a team of approximately five to six purchasing professionals, establishing clear responsibilities, performance expectations, and accountability.
 Organize and prioritize departmental workloads to ensure purchasing activities are aligned with operational demands and business priorities.
 Establish individual and departmental performance objectives, monitor results, and provide ongoing feedback and performance management.
 Identify training and development opportunities to strengthen procurement capabilities, negotiation skills, supplier management, and purchasing effectiveness.
 Reporting, Compliance & Risk Management 
 Develop and maintain purchasing reports and dashboards to monitor procurement expenditures, supplier performance, cost savings, purchase order activity, and purchasing trends.
 Ensure purchasing activities comply with company policies, established approval authorities, contractual obligations, and applicable regulatory requirements.
 Maintain accurate and complete purchasing documentation to support financial controls, internal reviews, and audit requirements.
 Identify and address procurement-related risks, including supplier dependency, pricing volatility, supplier reliability, and commercial exposure.
 Promote ethical purchasing practices, supplier transparency, and appropriate management of potential conflicts of interest.
 What You'll Bring: 
 Skills and Competencies: 
 Continuous improvement mindset with attention to detail
 Strong communication and vendor management skills
 Knowledge of supply chain processes and inventory management
 Excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills
 Technical skills that would be an asset:
 Lean / Six Sigma
 Proficiency in procurement software and Microsoft Office
 Inventory planning
 Education and Experience: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or related field
 SCMP, CPSM, an asset
 5+ years proven experience in procurement or purchasing
 What We Offer: 
 Competitive salary
 Retirement savings plan with employer contributions up to 6%
 Dynamic team within a high-growth company
 Company events and team-building activities
 Ongoing training and professional development opportunities
 TELUS Virtual Health Care with 24/7 access.
 Through  our partnership with OPUS, you can save on your daily commute. Employees receive 35% off the regular monthly Zone A transit pass. 
 Candidates will be required to undergo a background and reference check prior to hiring.
 The ability to communicate in French with our Quebec team is important.We operate in a multicultural and international environment, so strong English skills are also required to collaborate effectively with our suppliers and global team.

JOB DESCRIPTION: 
 À propos d’Abbott 
 Abbott est un chef de file mondial de l’industrie des soins de santé qui crée des solutions scientifiques révolutionnaires visant à améliorer la santé des gens. L’entreprise est résolument tournée vers l’avenir, à l’affût des changements qui pourraient survenir dans le domaine des sciences et des technologies médicales.
 Être à l’emploi d’Abbott 
 En étant à l’emploi d’Abbott, vous pourrez faire un travail qui compte, vous perfectionner et apprendre, prendre soin de vous et des membres de votre famille, rester fidèle à ce que vous êtes et vivre pleinement. Vous pourrez :
 profiter de possibilités d’avancement professionnel au sein d’une entreprise internationale qui vous permettra de bâtir la carrière dont vous rêvez;
 travailler pour une entreprise reconnue dans des douzaines de pays partout dans le monde comme étant un excellent milieu de travail et figurant parmi les entreprises les plus admirées dans le monde dans le classement Fortune;
 travailler pour une grande entreprise reconnue comme étant l’une des meilleures où travailler, notamment pour ce qui a trait à la diversité du personnel, à la conciliation travail-famille ainsi qu’à la place des femmes dans les postes de cadres et les postes scientifiques.
 L’occasion à saisir 
 Le Chef, Relations avec les parties prenantes travaillera pour Abbott Soins du diabète.  
 Ce que vous ferez  
 La personne titulaire du poste de chef des Relations avec les parties prenantes (Québec et Canada atlantique) est chargée d’établir et d’entretenir des relations stratégiques avec les principales parties prenantes externes au Québec, au Nouveau-Brunswick, en Nouvelle-Écosse, à l’Île-du-Prince-Édouard et à Terre-Neuve-et-Labrador. Cela comprend des interactions avec les représentants des gouvernements provinciaux (tant politiques qu’administratifs), les ministères de la Santé, les organismes chargés de l’évaluation des technologies de la santé et de l’élaboration des politiques, les professionnels de la santé, les leaders d’opinion clés, les groupes de défense des intérêts des patients ainsi que les associations professionnelles du secteur. Ce poste vise principalement à favoriser la réalisation des objectifs de l’entreprise en matière d’accès au marché, de politiques et d’affaires, grâce à une démarche proactive de défense des intérêts des parties prenantes. Le ou la chef dirige l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de stratégies régionales auprès des parties prenantes, repère les occasions d’influencer les décisions en matière de politiques et de financement, et établit des partenariats qui favorisent l’accès des patients à des solutions de soins de santé innovantes. De plus, la personne titulaire du poste fournit en temps opportun des renseignements et des analyses stratégiques à la direction, élabore des présentations et des documents d’information de grande qualité, et répond avec célérité aux besoins des parties prenantes et aux enjeux émergents afin d’assurer l’alignement avec les priorités de l’entreprise au Québec et dans le Canada atlantique.
 Stratégie d’accès au marché et mise en œuvre 
 Soutenir l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de stratégies provinciales d’accès au marché afin de faire progresser les objectifs de remboursement, de financement et d’accès des patients pour la gamme de produits d’Abbott Soins du diabète au Québec et dans le Canada atlantique.
 Évaluer les tendances, les priorités en matière de financement et les parcours d’accès des systèmes de santé provinciaux afin de cerner les occasions et les risques ayant une incidence sur l’accès aux technologies et aux solutions d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Interactions avec les parties prenantes – Accès au marché 
 Établir et entretenir des relations stratégiques avec les principales parties prenantes au Québec et dans le Canada atlantique, notamment les payeurs publics et privés, les professionnels de la santé, les leaders d’opinion clés, les décideurs des systèmes de santé, les parties prenantes de l’évaluation des technologies de la santé, les groupes de défense des intérêts des patients, les associations sectorielles et les représentants gouvernementaux.
 Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des plans de mobilisation des parties prenantes favorisant le financement, le remboursement et l’adoption de technologies et de solutions d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Représenter Abbott Soins du diabète dans les interactions avec les parties prenantes et tirer parti de leurs perspectives pour orienter les stratégies d’accès au marché, la planification commerciale et les priorités en matière d’accès.
 Soutien à l’évaluation des technologies de la santé et au remboursement 
 Appuyer les initiatives liées à l’évaluation des technologies de la santé, au remboursement et au financement concernant de la gamme de produits d’Abbotts Soins du diabète grâce à des renseignements sur les parties prenantes, à des analyses du contexte et à des perspectives stratégiques.
 Surveiller et évaluer les facteurs qui influencent les décisions en matière de remboursement, de liste des médicaments et de financement, et formuler des recommandations visant à optimiser l’accès des patients aux technologies d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Défense des intérêts des patients et partenariats avec les systèmes de santé 
 Établir et entretenir des partenariats avec des associations de patients et des parties prenantes du secteur de la santé afin de soutenir des initiatives visant à améliorer les résultats pour les personnes vivant avec le diabète et à élargir l’accès aux solutions d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Cerner les occasions de mener des actions collaboratives de défense des intérêts et de mettre en œuvre des initiatives liées aux systèmes de santé qui correspondent aux priorités des patients, des payeurs et des systèmes de santé.
 Suivi des politiques de santé et veille stratégique 
 Suivre l’évolution des politiques de santé, des questions de remboursement, des budgets et de la législation au Québec et dans le Canada atlantique, susceptibles d’avoir une incidence sur l’accès aux technologies liées au diabète et sur la gamme de produits d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Fournir en temps opportun des analyses portant sur les changements de politiques, les points de vue des parties prenantes, les activités de la concurrence et les nouvelles tendances en matière d’accès, afin d’appuyer la prise de décisions stratégiques.
 Collaboration interfonctionnelle 
 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes Accès au marché, Affaires médicales, Division commerciale, Affaires réglementaires et Communications afin de faire progresser les priorités stratégiques des activités d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Agir en tant que ressource stratégique concernant les cadres provinciaux de remboursement, la dynamique des parties prenantes et les occasions d’accès au marché . 
 Communication stratégique et présentations pour la haute direction 
 Élaborer des documents d’information à l’intention de la haute direction, des présentations, des plans de mobilisation des parties prenantes et des mises à jour sur les politiques afin d’appuyer les objectifs d’accès aux marchés d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Fournir à la direction des mises à jour proactives concernant les activités des parties prenantes, les occasions à saisir, les risques et les principaux développements
 Gestion du budget et des agences 
 Gérer les consultants externes, les agences et les budgets afin de soutenir l’engagement des parties prenantes et les priorités d’accès au marché pour la gamme de produits d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Financement de l’innovation et solutions d’accès 
 Définir et promouvoir des modèles de financement innovants, des partenariats dans le domaine de la santé et des solutions d’accès qui favorisent un accès durable des patients aux technologies d’Abbott Soins du diabète et s’alignent sur les priorités du système de santé.
 Collaborer avec les parties prenantes internes et externes pour explorer des occasions répondant aux besoins non comblés en matière de soins du diabète et améliorer l’accès à des technologies innovantes au Québec et dans le Canada atlantique
 Compétences requises 
 Exigences en matière de formation :
 Baccalauréat (obligatoire) : 
 Dans un domaine pertinent tel que les politiques publiques, l’évaluation des technologies de la santé, l’économie de la santé, les sciences politiques, la communication, l’administration des affaires ou la gestion des soins de santé
 Maîtrise ou doctorat (souhaitable, mais non obligatoire) : 
 En politiques publiques, économie de la santé, évaluation des technologies de la santé, administration des affaires (MBA) ou dans un domaine lié à la santé, afin de démontrer une compréhension approfondie tant des politiques publiques que du paysage du secteur des soins de santé
 Certifications supplémentaires (facultatives, mais avantageuses) : 
 Certifications professionnelles en gestion des parties prenantes, affaires publiques ou relations gouvernementales 
 Le ou la titulaire du poste doit pouvoir bien communiquer en anglais (50% du temps), car ses fonctions exigent des interactions avec des intervenants et collègues se trouvant à l’extérieur du Québec ou du Canada
 Expérience requise de 5 ans à moins de 8 ans
 Expérience avérée dans la gestion des relations avec les parties prenantes, les relations gouvernementales, les affaires publiques ou les relations externes au sein du secteur de la santé, des dispositifs médicaux ou de l’industrie pharmaceutique
 Les candidats peuvent fournir des exemples de réalisations en collaboration avec des parties prenantes externes clés, telles que les représentants gouvernementaux, les organismes d’évaluation des technologies de santé, les professionnels de santé et les associations de patients
 Expérience en matière de politiques publiques et de défense des intérêts : solide compréhension des politiques publiques, de l’évaluation des technologies de santé et des environnements réglementaires. Une expérience de la collaboration avec les décideurs publics et les organisations de défense des intérêts est essentielle 
 Établissement de relations stratégiques : vaste expérience dans la création et le maintien de relations professionnelles à long terme avec un éventail diversifié de parties prenantes
 Capacité à travailler sous pression et à agir rapidement : expérience avérée dans des environnements au rythme soutenu, où il est essentiel de réagir rapidement aux situations urgentes et de gérer des priorités en constante évolution
 Excellentes compétences en communication et en présentation : capacité démontrée à élaborer des présentations de grande qualité, à formuler des messages clairs et à communiquer efficacement avec les parties prenantes internes et externes, y compris la haute direction
 Gestion de projets et supervision des ressources : expérience dans la gestion d’agences ou de consultants externes, de budgets et de projets comportant de multiples parties prenantes, en veillant à l’harmonisation avec les objectifs stratégiques
 Connaissance du secteur de la santé : familiarité avec l’écosystème de la santé, notamment les payeurs, les professionnels de la santé et les cadres d’accès au marché. Une expérience préalable au sein d’une entreprise de dispositifs médicaux ou de biotechnologie est vivement souhaitée

In 1977, Charles and Ray Eames began a film with a picnic beside Chicago’s lakefront. Over the next nine minutes, Powers of Ten traveled out toward distant galaxies and back into the microscopic world inside a human hand. An enormous subject became a journey you could follow, built around a simple change in perspective. Images, language, movement, and sound brought the idea to life together. 
 That’s the kind of creative thinking we’re looking for at Mercury: finding a compelling idea inside something complex, then bringing together the people and crafts that make it unforgettable.
 We’re looking for a Group Creative Director to build and lead Brand Narrative , a new team within Brand Creative. You’ll turn company strategy, product truths, customer insight, and cultural observations into original concepts for our most important launches, campaigns, and brand moments. You’ll originate ideas yourself and stay closely involved as they become finished work.
 Your background might be in art direction, design, or copywriting. What matters is your ability to develop exceptional concepts, recognize the best idea wherever it comes from, and bring the whole creative studio together to make it real. Whatever your starting discipline, you’ll bring deep experience in film-led storytelling.
 You’ll lead Brand Narrative in close creative partnership with your peers leading Brand Design and Writing. Together, you’ll shape concepts, language, and visual expression from the beginning, bringing distinct perspectives and shared ownership to the work. You’ll contribute strong ideas of your own, invite others to challenge and improve them, and build on theirs. This is a role for someone who enjoys making work together, not developing ideas in isolation and handing them off.
 You’ll also shape what Brand Narrative becomes. That means building its culture, developing its people, and establishing ways of working that make the entire studio more creatively ambitious. The opportunity is to make great work while building a team that can keep making it.
 What you’ll do
 In your first year, your focus will be roughly 70% leading creative development for our highest-priority launches and campaigns, and 30% building the Brand Narrative function. 
 Originate and lead big creative ideas. Partner with Product Marketing and Brand Marketing on the brief, then turn the agreed audience, opportunity, and product proof into original creative concepts. Develop ideas that can take distinctive forms across film, social, out-of-home, digital, experiences, and partnerships.
 Bring ambitious concepts to life with your creative peers and the full studio. Work side by side with the Brand Design and Writing leads and their teams from the earliest explorations through delivery. Develop ideas together, exchange thoughtful critique, and make creative choices that draw on each discipline’s expertise. Stay hands-on, contribute through your own craft, and partner closely with Motion and Production throughout. For film, remain closely involved through scripts, visual development, production, and the final edit.
 Build audience and distribution thinking into the idea. Shape concepts around how people will discover, watch, and share the work. Work with marketing partners to consider channels and viewing contexts from the beginning, so the work belongs where people encounter it rather than simply being resized to fit.
 Push beyond the first good answer, and learn quickly. Lead thoughtful concept development and critique. Use rough scripts, prototypes, and AI tools to test ideas quickly, learn, and move the strongest work forward. Know when to keep exploring and when to commit, then protect what makes an idea interesting through feedback and production.
 Find opportunities before a brief arrives. Bring curiosity about Mercury’s products, customers, and the wider world. Develop proactive ideas and cultural opportunities that give the brand something meaningful to say or do.
 Help decide where creative ambition matters most. Partner early with Product Marketing, Brand Marketing, Product Design, Comms, and Insights. Help identify which moments deserve our largest creative investment, present recommendations to senior leadership, and use results from marketing and insights partners to inform what comes next.
 Build and lead Brand Narrative. Define the team’s purpose, priorities, creative standards, and ways of working. Help hire and develop the team, shaping its structure and capabilities. Set clear expectations, and coach people to grow their judgment and conceptual strength.
 Create a culture where the best idea wins. Make room for experimentation, honest feedback, and contributions across disciplines. Lead with generosity and conviction, share ownership of the work, and help people challenge one another without making creativity a competition for credit.
 Build practices that strengthen the work. Establish a clear path from insight and an agreed brief to concept and execution, with useful critique and close collaboration throughout. Develop relationships with external creatives and agencies who can add a distinctive perspective or capability when needed.
 What you’ll bring
 A strong creative foundation in art direction, design, or copywriting. Your portfolio shows original concepts developed into ambitious, well-crafted work across multiple formats. You can explain what you contributed, how the idea evolved, and how collaboration made it better.
 Deep film experience. You’ve developed film-led ideas from concept through production, with strong instincts for story, scripts, performance, pacing, and sound. You understand how these choices work together to make an audience feel something, not just make a film look good.
 A track record of deep creative collaboration with design and writing peers. You’ve led ambitious multidisciplinary work from concept through production by building trusted partnerships. You bring a clear point of view, listen closely, work through creative disagreements constructively, and recognize when someone else’s approach makes the work stronger. You can show how your collaborators shaped the outcome, not just what you personally originated.
 Strong taste, cultural awareness, and product curiosity. You can get close to a complex business or product, find the human truth within it, and turn that understanding into something clear, surprising, and memorable.
 Experience developing creative people and shaping how a team works. You give specific, useful feedback, set a high bar with care, and create an environment where people can take creative risks. You’re excited to build a new function, including the everyday practices that give it a culture.
 Clear communication and sound judgment. You can rally people around an ambitious concept, explain why it deserves investment, and navigate competing perspectives without losing the idea. You take ownership in ambiguous situations and balance creative ambition with the need to move work forward.
 What success looks like
 A year in, you’ll have led major launches and film-led campaigns from original concept through finished work, with Brand Design and Writing as creative partners from the beginning. The studio’s disciplines will have shaped the work together, with audience and distribution informing the creative approach.
 Brand Narrative will have a clear identity, shared creative standards, and working practices that help people test and develop stronger ideas together. Alongside planned launches, you’ll have established a pipeline of proactive opportunities that gives Mercury more ways to express its product ambition with originality and cultural relevance.
 Please include a portfolio featuring film-led work and broader campaign concepts. We’d love to understand your role in developing the ideas, the choices you made through production, and how you brought the work to life with others.

À propos de Mila 
 Fondé par le professeur Yoshua Bengio de l’Université de Montréal, Mila rassemble des chercheurs spécialisés en intelligence artificielle (IA) et plus précisément en apprentissage automatique. Reconnu mondialement pour ses importantes contributions aux domaines de l’apprentissage profond et apprentissage par renforcement, Mila s’est particulièrement distingué dans la modélisation du langage, la traduction automatique, la reconnaissance d’objets et les modèles génératifs. Depuis 2017, Mila est le fruit d’une collaboration entre l’Université de Montréal et l’Université McGill, en lien étroit avec Polytechnique Montréal et HEC Montréal.
Mila s’est donné pour mission d’être un pôle mondial d’avancées scientifiques qui inspire l’innovation et l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle pour le bénéfice de tous.
 À propos du poste et de votre future équipe  
 Sous la responsabilité du Directeur principal - Recherche appliquée, vous serez chargé.e de conduire la réussite des projets de l’équipe interne de recherche appliquée de Mila. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les chercheur.e.s, les équipes de développement IA et de définition produit, ainsi qu’avec diverses parties prenantes internes et externes à Mila.
 Dans ce rôle clé, vous superviserez la planification, l’exécution et la livraison de projets de recherche de pointe, tout en veillant à leur alignement avec les objectifs stratégiques de Mila et aux plus hauts standards de qualité scientifique. Vous assumerez la gestion et le mentorat d’équipes diversifiées de chercheur.e.s dans un environnement collaboratif et innovant. Votre leadership sera essentiel pour faciliter une communication fluide avec nos partenaires et propulser l’application de solutions d’IA face à des défis concrets, faisant ainsi progresser la science et l’industrie vers un impact positif au niveau économique et sociétal.
 Vos principales responsabilités 
 Gestion de projets et livraison : Piloter l'exécution opérationnelle des projets de recherche appliquée, du cadrage initial jusqu'à la livraison. Assurer le suivi des livrables définis conjointement avec les responsables techniques (tech leads) et responsables produit (product managers), la maîtrise des budgets, le respect des échéanciers et la conformité avec les énoncés de travaux. Assurer l’amélioration continue des méthodes d’organisation agiles du travail et éliminer les obstacles opérationnels pour maximiser la fluidité du travail des équipes.
 Gestion proactive des partenariats et gouvernance : Agir comme point de contact principal pour la gouvernance de la relation projet avec les clients et collaborateurs. Traduire et aligner les attentes d'affaires avec les impératifs scientifiques, tout en assurant une communication fluide et un niveau élevé de satisfaction.
 Leadership et développement des personnes : Encadrer, soutenir et mentorer l'équipe de chercheur.e.s au quotidien. Assurer la gestion du talent, favoriser un environnement collaboratif et veiller au développement professionnel des membres de l'équipe.
 Coordination transversale et innovation : Facilitateur central entre la recherche appliquée, les équipes de développement IA et le l’équipe de définition produit. Se maintenir à l'affût des avancées en IA pour soutenir l'innovation et garantir le positionnement de pointe de l'organisation.
 Qualifications recherchées 
 Expérience pertinente: Minimum de 5 à 7 années d’expérience dans un rôle similaire (ex. gestion de projets de recherche/développement en IA, gestion d'équipes techniques ou livraison de solutions logicielles complexes).
 Gestion de projet: Maîtrise d’une méthode de gestion de projet scientifique et expérience avérée dans la facilitation des activités d'équipes pluridisciplinaires.
 Culture technique en IA: Solide compréhension des concepts d'apprentissage automatique (ML) et d'IA, avec la capacité de dialoguer efficacement avec des chercheur.e.s et des développeurs.
 Gestion de livrables et contrats: Expérience concrète dans la livraison de projets avec des clients corporatifs, incluant le suivi des énoncés de travaux, le respect des budgets et la gestion des échéanciers.
 Gestion des parties prenantes: Excellente capacité à établir et maintenir des relations de confiance avec une diversité d'intervenants (chercheur.e.s, équipes de développement, responsable produit et partenaires industriels).
 Leadership et communication: Leadership collaboratif, aptitudes pour le mentorat d'équipe et excellente capacité à vulgariser des concepts techniques complexes auprès d'un public non technologique.

The Director, Global Supply Chain Strategy & Architecture is responsible for defining the long-term strategy and future-state architecture of the global Supply Chain organization.
 This leader will translate business growth objectives, product strategy, customer requirements, market dynamics, and external supply-chain trends into an integrated global supply chain strategy and future-state design. The role will define the strategic choices required across the supply chain network, manufacturing and partner ecosystem, capacity, resilience, inventory positioning, and critical capabilities to ensure the Supply Chain is positioned to scale, respond, and perform as the business evolves.
 The Director will serve as the architect and integrator of the end-to-end supply chain , connecting functional strategies into a cohesive future-state direction, identifying structural and capability requirements, developing strategic scenarios, and establishing the multi-year roadmap required to prepare Supply Chain for future business needs.
 Key Responsibilities 
 1. Global Supply Chain Strategy 
 Lead the development and ongoing evolution of the global, multi-year Supply Chain strategy , aligned with the corporate strategy and growth objectives.
 Translate business, product, market, and customer strategies into implications for the future supply chain.
 Define the strategic choices required across areas such as global footprint, capacity, sourcing, manufacturing, inventory, logistics, supply assurance, resilience, and partner strategy.
 Identify the capabilities required to enable the supply chain to scale effectively while maintaining agility, competitiveness, and customer responsiveness.
 Maintain an external perspective on geopolitical developments, industry trends, supply-market dynamics, manufacturing models, and emerging supply-chain practices.
 2. Physical Strategic Roadmap & Prioritization 
 Develop and maintain an integrated 3-5 year Supply Chain strategic roadmap , translating strategy into clear priorities and strategic initiatives.
 Establish the strategic rationale and expected business outcomes associated with major supply-chain investments.
 Identify dependencies and trade-offs across major strategic initiatives and recommend priorities
 Ensure functional strategies connect to a common end-to-end direction rather than developing independently.
 Partner with functional leaders to translate the global strategy into actionable priorities within their respective organizations.
 Facilitate leadership discussions and strategy sessions focused on major supply-chain choices and priorities.
 Establish a regular cadence for reviewing the Supply Chain strategy, external assumptions, strategic risks, and progress against priorities.
 Ensure strategic decisions are translated into clear ownership and accountability across the Supply Chain organization.
 3. Supply Chain Network & Ecosystem Strategy 
 Develop strategic perspectives on the global supply-chain footprint and ecosystem required to support future growth.
 Assess long-term requirements for manufacturing capacity, geographic diversification, supplier ecosystem, contract manufacturing, distribution, and logistics networks.
 Evaluate strategic make/buy/partner considerations and recommend the appropriate operating model for different elements of the supply chain.
 Incorporate geopolitical, concentration, continuity, capacity, cost, and customer considerations into global network decisions.
 Partner with functional leaders to develop strategies that strengthen supply assurance and reduce structural supply-chain risk.
 4. Strategic Capacity & Scale Readiness 
 Assess the supply chain's ability to support future revenue, product, volume, and customer requirements.
 Identify structural constraints that could limit the company's ability to scale.
 Develop strategic scenarios for different growth, demand, supply, and geopolitical conditions.
 Identify where additional capacity, capability, supplier diversification, inventory, or ecosystem investment may be required.
 Establish a forward-looking view of supply-chain readiness and bring recommended actions and trade-offs to senior leadership.
 5. Strategic Business & Financial Analysis 
 Develop fact-based recommendations for complex supply-chain decisions, clearly articulating options, trade-offs, risks, investment requirements, and expected business outcomes .
 Develop business cases for significant strategic supply-chain investments and decisions.
 Partner with Finance to assess the financial implications of alternative supply-chain strategies.
 Balance service, growth, resilience, inventory, working capital, cost, and investment considerations when developing strategic recommendations.
 Establish measures that demonstrate whether the supply-chain strategy is delivering the intended business outcomes.
 6.  Enterprise & Cross-Functional Alignment 
 Build strong partnerships across Product Line Management (PLM), R&D, Finance, Sales Operations, and other Enterprise functions.
 Connect product roadmaps, business growth plans, financial objectives, and customer requirements to future supply-chain requirements.
 Ensure Supply Chain implications are incorporated early into major business and product decisions.
 Outside the Scope of This Role 
 This role does not own: 
 Digital supply-chain strategy or technology implementation
 Process transformation and process redesign
 Supply-chain systems implementation
 Automation or AI deployment
 Transformation program management
 Day-to-day functional or operational execution
 The Must Haves: 
 Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related discipline.
 Significant progressive experience in global supply chain, operations, strategy, or a related leadership role.
 Broad end-to-end understanding of supply-chain disciplines including planning, sourcing, manufacturing, inventory, logistics, supplier management, and supply assurance.
 Demonstrated ability to develop long-term strategy and translate complex business requirements into clear strategic priorities.
 Experience within a complex global manufacturing environment, ideally technology, telecommunications, electronics, semiconductor, or a related sector.
 Experience evaluating supply-chain networks, manufacturing strategies, capacity requirements, outsourcing models, and/or global supply ecosystems.
 Strong business and financial acumen with experience developing investment recommendations and evaluating strategic trade-offs.
 Exceptional executive communication skills and demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders across organizational boundaries.
 Nice to have: 
 MBA or advanced degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Finance, or related discipline.
 Experience working within an outsourced or contract-manufacturing operating model.
 Experience supporting periods of significant business growth or structural change.
 Experience with scenario planning, network strategy, supply-chain risk, and global capacity strategy.
 Leadership Competencies 
 Enterprise Thinking: Optimizes decisions for the end-to-end business rather than individual functions.
 Strategic Foresight: Anticipates future business requirements and their implications for the supply chain.
 Commercial Acumen: Connects supply-chain choices directly to growth, customers and financial outcomes.
 Structured Problem Solving: Brings clarity and fact-based thinking to ambiguous strategic issues.
 Influence & Alignment: Builds commitment across functions and senior leaders.
 Executive Presence: Communicates complex strategic issues simply and confidently.
 Decision Orientation: Moves strategy beyond analysis into clear choices, priorities, and accountability.

The salary range for this role in the eastern-USA is $158, 800 - $253, 600

ROLE SUMMARY 
 Applied Intelligence is the zero-to-one function of Pfizer’s commercial data science organization. It takes ambiguous, high-value AI and machine learning problems in the commercial business, proves whether they can be solved and whether solving them is worth it, builds the first working version to production standards, and graduates it to the product team that will own and scale it. First versions are built to be understood, reproduced, and extended by teams who did not write them.
 As a Senior Manager, AI Engineer, you build the systems behind those first versions: the services, pipelines, agent runtimes, and data contracts that turn a proven idea into something that runs, can be trusted, and can be handed over. Current priorities include agentic decision systems that choose which healthcare professionals and consumers to reach, through which channels, and when. These systems take in new data as it arrives, keep track of what has happened and what is still pending, reason over the options, act through channels such as field teams, email, and digital media, and check whether the action worked. Large language models and agents are part of the design where their cost is justified, machine learning models carry the stable, well-defined parts of the problem, and much of the work is careful software and data engineering.
 This is a hands-on individual contributor role with informal technical leadership. You will own the architecture of a first-version system or a major component of one, set the engineering bar through code review and example, and write much of the core code yourself.  Sadie is building voice AI for restaurants. Our voice AI host answers restaurant phones 24/7, takes reservations and takeout orders, and answers guest questions. It connects to the restaurant's reservation system and POS, so every call becomes a booking or an order and staff can stay focused on service.
 We're looking for a bilingual (French and English) Customer Success Manager to get new restaurants live on Sadie and make sure they keep getting value after launch. You'll own each customer from kickoff through go-live and ongoing adoption. You'll plan the onboarding, coordinate setup and integrations, train managers and staff, and decide when a restaurant is ready to launch. After go-live, you'll watch usage and call performance and step in when adoption slips.
 AI should be part of how you work. Use it to draft, research, analyze and automate parts of your workflow so you have more time for customers. You're responsible for the quality of the result.
 What we value
 Following through on what you told a customer you'd do.
 Sound judgment when needs, priorities or timelines change.
 Staying calm when a customer is frustrated or the next step is unclear.
 Sharing context and asking questions openly.
 Questioning assumptions, including your own.
 What you'll do
 Get each restaurant live 
 You're the main point of contact for new customers from kickoff through go-live. Take the handoff from Sales so you know the restaurant's goals, expectations, key contacts and implementation requirements. Build the onboarding plan with timelines, responsibilities, dependencies and go-live milestones, and keep communication clear and next steps agreed.
 Gather and validate the restaurant information and workflows Sadie needs. Coordinate account setup, integrations with booking and point-of-sale (POS) systems, and configuration of Sadie's voice features, bringing in technical teams when you need them.
 Decide when a restaurant is ready to launch 
 Before launch, coordinate checks of account setup, integrations and representative call scenarios, and track every issue through to resolution. Confirm the restaurant is ready, with setup complete, staff trained, launch expectations set and support routes clear.
 The operator buys Sadie, but the guest is the one calling. Guests never chose Sadie and just want a table or an order. If the call goes badly, the restaurant wears it, so you don't sign off on a launch you aren't confident in.
 Train managers and staff 
 Run virtual onboarding sessions and practical training for restaurant managers and staff, in French or English. Tailor each session to the team's needs and how comfortable they are with technology, so they feel confident on launch day.
 Build adoption after go-live 
 Monitor usage, call performance and customer health to spot adoption gaps, emerging risks and chances to improve. Reach out with best practices, configuration recommendations and follow-up training before customers have to ask.
 Stay a trusted advisor. Review progress against each customer's goals and help them get the most out of Sadie.
 Keep records and feed what you learn back to the team 
 Work with Sales, Support and Product on handoffs, escalations and customer updates, with clear ownership and follow-through. Track onboarding timelines, go-live milestones, adoption and customer health, and tell the right people about progress and risks.
 Keep clear customer records of goals, configuration decisions, onboarding progress, open issues and agreed next steps. Share customer insights, recurring problems and feedback with Product. Improve onboarding documentation, training materials and customer success playbooks so every restaurant gets a consistent experience as Sadie grows.
 What you'll bring
 Fluent French and English. French proficiency is essential.
 1+ years in customer success, onboarding, implementation, account management or a similar customer-facing technology role.
 Experience guiding customers through software onboarding, implementation or adoption.
